results.notes: Outcome paragraph_clarity; treatment=reranking, control=none. All computed means, SDs, differences and SEs use the original 0-100 paragraph-rating scale. The reported percent attenuation is a reproduction benchmark, not the unit of the new contrast. No unaided-paragraph score is subtracted from the participant outcome. Reader ratings are averaged within the final AI paragraph, then within writer and condition; each writer has one proposition per condition, and every writer receives equal weight. SDs use n-1. The paper's preferred subset replaces unedited AI text with edited text wherever available and excludes writer-proposition pairs with writer_preference='original'; equal and edited preferences are retained. These are post-treatment preference restrictions, so these contrasts describe the retained sample rather than all randomized writers. The reproduction sample has 19102 reader-paragraph rows, 730 distinct writers, and 2543 readers. Reranking has 3085 ratings of 603 writers; none has 3262 ratings of 648 writers before pair completion. Reproduction uses an independently fitted beta/logit mixed model with reader random intercepts, all four categories (unaided writer, none, prompting, reranking), and y=((rating/100)*(N-1)+0.5)/N. Average marginal effects use random effects set to zero, as in the authors' marginaleffects re.form=NA specification. Maximum absolute likelihood gradient=5.1571369e-05. The downloaded supplement is dated October 8, 2026 and has a changed title; it is later than the saved arXiv v2 of June 29, 2026. Its Study 3 sample, models, interventions, counts, and reader-only regression specification match the saved main paper and posted data. Its Section 8.5 and Tables S286-S290 provide numerical benchmarks where the main paper has only figures. The main-paper clarity effect also reproduces at -26.9 percent, providing a direct version cross-check. No figure values are used. This outcome's benchmarks come from supplement PDF p.200, Table S287; all counts and model checks refer to the full published analysis. No printed outcome-specific distinct-writer counts or first-round statistics are available. Paired analysis retains only writers with both eligible reranking and none outcomes. The difference is the mean within-writer difference; its SE is SD(within-writer differences)/sqrt(number of complete pairs). Both arm SDs are computed over exactly those same paired writers.
